intended_use: Reusable HIL and physical-test planning matrix for grid-forming converter and microgrid systems. Exact acceptance thresholds must be set by the selected published standard, interconnection agreement and mission specification.
comparison_policy: A topology may claim only the operating modes it has actually tested.
Grid-following behavior does not establish grid-forming capability.
Black-start requires starting from a declared dead-bus state without external grid supply, including required auxiliaries.
A component pass does not establish microgrid-controller, protection or system-level pass.
Simulation/HIL results must be labelled as such and kept separate from physical hardware test receipts.
No universal voltage, frequency, ROCOF, THD or recovery limits are invented by this catalogue.
All test thresholds must cite the applicable standard edition, utility interconnection agreement or mission acceptance criteria.
Record waveform sample rates, instrument calibration, measurement point, configuration SHA and uncertainty.

sources.title: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), Performance Evaluation of a Single-Phase Grid-Forming Inverter Through Hardware Experiments
sources.notes: Published under the laboratory's former NREL name in October 2024; the laboratory was renamed National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) effective 1 December 2025. Research test protocol and example inverter results, not universal standards acceptance limits.

sources.publisher: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL)
sources.notes: Current NLR research page describing grid black start, auxiliary start supply, microgrid restoration and grid-forming inverter support.

Open Compute Project Data Center Facility Power Distribution

sources.title: The State of Energy Innovation 2026
sources.notes: Grid-forming inverter development, deployments and interoperability/standards maturity.

sources.title: UNIFI 1-MW Multi-Vendor Grid-Forming Inverter Test Updates
sources.notes: Presentation authored under the National Renewable Energy Laboratory name before its 1 Dec 2025 renaming to National Laboratory of the Rockies. Five integration scenarios combine up to 7 GFM inverters (760 kVA), 4 GFL inverters (340 kVA), one synchronous genset and controllable loads; test matrix explores 0–100% inverter-based resources and 0–69% GFM share. Report notes ROCOF failures at 68% and 100% GFM asset-mix scenarios and unequal power sharing/instability in the highest-GFM case.

sources.title: UNIFI Specifications for Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources: Version 3
sources.publisher: National Laboratory of the Rockies / UNIFI Consortium
sources.notes: Defines vendor-agnostic system-level and inverter-functional requirements. The V3 programme adds frequency-domain criteria and quantitative pass/fail tests; use the exact document tables, model assumptions and test clauses for limits. No thresholds are paraphrased or invented here.

sources.title: IEEE P2800.1 — Recommended Practice for Functional Capabilities and Performance of Grid-Forming Equipment in IBR/CBR
sources.notes: Active PAR approved 10 December 2025. Complements IEEE 2800; covers technical minimum GFM capabilities/performance and model-based test procedures/criteria for power-electronic IBR/CBR equipment. Does not apply to GFM equipment without a power-electronic interface.

sources.title: IEEE 2800.2-2026 — Recommended Practice for Test and Verification Procedures for Inverter-Based Resources Interconnecting with Bulk Power Systems
sources.notes: Published 30 June 2026. Defines plant-level conformity assessment procedures to verify IEEE 2800 conformity for IBR plants interconnected to transmission/sub-transmission bulk power systems. Distinct from P2800.1 and from microgrid-controller / islanded operation standards.

sources.title: Review of Industry Efforts and Standards: Data Center Design for IT Load Protection
sources.notes: Published white paper covering AC/DC/hybrid distribution, redundancy/load priority, system/personnel protection, AI workload consumption patterns, disturbance response, cooling and grid interaction. Identifies need for measurable interoperability definitions.

sources.title: Data Centers: Standards Needs Analysis and Recommendations
sources.notes: IEEE identifies fast-changing data-centre load time constants, grid-interconnection challenges, local power needs, microgrids, forecasting uncertainty and co-location as standards needs.

sources.title: Spatially Correlated Load Dynamics in AI Data-Center-Dominated Grids
sources.notes: Real-time EMT simulation on IEEE 39-bus system. Reported correlated AI data-centre loading increases aggregate active-power variability about 7x and frequency standard deviation about 11x versus an independent-load reference in the studied cases. These are study-specific simulation comparisons, not universal constants.

sources.title: Characterization of High-Resolution AI Data Center Training Workloads on Single and Multiple GPU Nodes
sources.notes: Open dataset with 32 training sessions on H100/B200 eight-GPU nodes and 40 sessions on RTX 3060 systems; over 1.8 million samples, 50 Hz where detailed traces are provided. Fields include CPU/GPU utilization, per-GPU power, memory and temperature. Not a geographically distributed fleet dataset; do not infer cross-site covariance from this source alone.

sources.title: Data Center Workload Flexibility for Power System Demand Response: Evidence from Alibaba Traces
sources.publisher: International Journal of Electrical Power & Energy Systems
sources.notes: Uses Alibaba cluster traces with more than one million tasks. The study estimates around 20% of data-centre power is associated with latency-tolerant tasks and reports up to 22% load shedding during flexibility windows under its LAD-Flex model. This is trace-based/modelled flexibility, not a field demonstration.

sources.title: AI Data Centres as Grid-Interactive Assets
sources.notes: Field demonstration on a 256-GPU cluster in a hyperscale cloud facility in Phoenix. Software-based workload orchestration reduced power by 25% for 3 hours during peak demand while maintaining declared AI QoS, without hardware changes or energy storage. This is a source-specific reference envelope, not a universal guaranteed flexibility level.

sources.title: Empirically-Calibrated H100 Node Power Models for Accurate AI Training Energy Estimation
sources.publisher: Environmental Research: Energy / Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
sources.notes: Empirical power model calibrated on measured H100 training loads; reports 11.4% MAPE and compares against TDP-based estimation errors of 27–37%. Use as a measurement/model calibration benchmark, not a universal across-hardware result.

sources.title: Wide-Area Power System Oscillations From Large-Scale AI Workloads
sources.notes: Develops dynamic AI data-centre load profiles and analyses sustained periodic stochastic training/fine-tuning power fluctuations as possible forcing inputs to local and inter-area oscillatory modes in WECC 179-bus and NPCC 140-bus simulations.

cases.name: multiple grid-forming converters with heterogeneous vendors
UNIFI 1 MW multi-vendor penetration sweep
cases.notes: Source-reported 1 MW multi-vendor HIL integration matrix. The 68% and 100% GFM asset-mixture cases failed the report's ROCOF test; the highest-GFM case exhibited the worst voltage/reactive-power interaction and unequal power sharing. More relaxed frequency droop (0.6% to 1.2%) allowed S4/S5 to survive the described ROCOF condition. These are study-specific findings, not general GFM thresholds or universal control settings.

test_groups.name: Protection and degraded-control behavior
test_groups.purpose: Validate coordination when inverter fault current is limited and remote controls fail.

cases.name: lost communications / stale or replayed control command

test_groups.name: DC-native bus service interface
test_groups.purpose: Test customer-load delivery at the declared DC bus rather than forcing all systems through an AC terminal.

cases.name: DC bus steady-state regulation and ripple
DC fault detection, selective isolation and restore

test_groups.name: Frequency-domain stability and impedance interaction
test_groups.purpose: Add UNIFI V3 frequency-domain capability assessment to the existing time-domain HIL matrix. Freeze the frequency band, operating point, model assumptions and pass/fail criteria from the applicable UNIFI V3 / IEEE project clause before testing.

cases.name: Converter sequence-impedance / admittance frequency scan
cases.scan_method: Use the frequency-domain perturbation and scan method specified by the selected UNIFI V3 clause; declare the injected signal, operating point, frequency band and measurement reference before test.
cases.frequency_band_policy: No universal band is hard-coded. Freeze the exact band from the applicable UNIFI V3 specification, model-validity envelope and declared system interaction frequencies.
cases.notes: Store the full complex frequency-response data, not just a pass/fail summary. Do not mix sequence-domain and dq-domain conventions without recording transforms and reference directions.

cases.name: Weak-grid converter-to-network impedance interaction
cases.scan_method: Repeat the declared frequency scan across a frozen set of grid-impedance / short-circuit-strength cases and operating points.
cases.frequency_band_policy: Frequency sweep and grid-strength points must follow the applicable UNIFI V3 / project acceptance source and the network model's declared validity range.
cases.notes: A stable time-domain step response does not replace small-signal frequency-domain assessment; reconcile the two evidence streams.

cases.name: Multi-vendor grid-forming control interaction scan
cases.scan_method: Scan individual devices and the combined fleet under the same frozen network and operating point; compare isolated and interconnected response.
cases.frequency_band_policy: Freeze frequency bands and pass/fail metrics from the UNIFI V3 clause and declared fleet/network use case.
cases.notes: Tests whether a multi-vendor mix creates emergent resonance or weak damping that is invisible in single-device testing.

test_groups.name: Data-centre IT-load protection and AI workload power transients
test_groups.purpose: Treat the data centre as a dynamic grid customer as well as an energy consumer. Test the end-to-end chain from grid point of connection through UPS, DC distribution and cooling to protected IT load, while exposing rapid AI workload ramps and power-quality disturbances.

cases.name: AI workload ramp and burst replay
preconditions: freeze workload/power trace and version
define IT load, rack bus and grid point-of-connection measurement points
record UPS, storage, converter and cooling state
cases.notes: Use a real anonymized workload-derived trace when permitted; otherwise label a synthetic trace. Do not infer grid impact from rack-level power alone.

cases.name: UPS and DC-bus ride-through during source disturbance
preconditions: declare AC/DC topology and bypass path
freeze critical and non-critical load priorities
declare energy reserve and autonomy target
cases.notes: Distinguish UPS ride-through, battery autonomy, source transfer and generator start. One does not prove the others.

cases.name: Load priority, shedding and restoration with cooling constraints
preconditions: declare critical IT tiers
declare cooling and thermal safety constraints
freeze restoration order and interlocks

cases.name: Grid disturbance and data-centre co-response
preconditions: declare grid code and utility operating envelope
freeze workload power caps and response policies
define no-break IT protection requirements
cases.notes: Measure the grid-facing response and IT-facing protection outcome together. A grid-support action must not silently compromise the protected IT service.

cases.name: Flexible-load dispatch without SLA or thermal violation
preconditions: define workload service-level agreement
declare thermal and cooling safety constraints
freeze allowed dispatch window and recovery obligations
cases.notes: A claimed demand-response resource must account for deferred work and rebound, not only instantaneous load reduction.

test_groups.name: Correlation-aware AI load modelling, grid oscillations and workload flexibility
test_groups.purpose: Model AI data-centre demand as a non-stationary, workload-driven, spatially correlated large electric load. Combine measured accelerator traces, multi-site common-mode correlation, grid dynamics and SLA-constrained workload flexibility. Do not assume independent sites or stationary Gaussian demand.

cases.name: Sub-second GPU workload trace ingestion and power-model holdout
preconditions: record hardware SKU, GPU count, firmware and power limits
freeze workload, batch-size, sequence-length and parallelization metadata
retain raw sampling timestamps and instrumentation calibration
cases.notes: The Scientific Data dataset is open and contains 72 sessions / 1.8M samples at 50 Hz. Evaluate against held-out workload families and hardware configurations. Initial target: beat the published 11.4% H100 model MAPE on its comparable domain; stretch target <8% MAPE with calibrated prediction intervals. Do not transfer H100 accuracy claims to B200/RTX without validation.

cases.name: Spatial correlation versus independent-site aggregation
preconditions: define fleet geography and electrical buses
declare shared model rollout, batch synchronization, cooling/weather and control events
freeze per-site marginal traces before applying correlation structures
cases.notes: The ~7x and ~11x figures are from one published system study. Use them as replication targets for its assumptions, not fixed universal multipliers. Required hostile control: independently randomize sites and show the model does not falsely preserve a common-mode correlation.

cases.name: Periodic workload forcing and grid modal interaction
preconditions: record workload periodicities and time-varying spectrum
freeze grid model and modal estimates
separate grid-control modes from workload forcing frequencies
cases.notes: Use stochastic and periodic training/fine-tuning traces to test local and inter-area modes. Include both grid-following and grid-forming supply cases; do not treat workload periodicity as white noise.

cases.name: Latency-aware demand response with SLA and rebound constraints
preconditions: classify workload latency tolerance and deadline
freeze SLA and work-completion accounting
include deferred queue, restart/checkpoint and cooling load
cases.notes: Alibaba-trace LAD-Flex study reports up to 22% load shedding during flexibility windows from modelled latency-tolerant demand. This is a trace-based benchmark; require same-window service completion, deadlines and rebound measurement.

cases.name: Field-reference workload flexibility envelope
preconditions: freeze exact workload mix and QoS contract
declare response notification and ramp profile
declare baseline energy use and workload completion denominator
cases.notes: Nature Energy field demonstration reported 25% reduction for 3 hours on a 256-GPU cluster while meeting declared QoS. Programme target: reproduce at matched workload/SLA, then stretch to >=30% for 3 hours without increased energy per completed work or rebound peak. This is a proposed target, not a guaranteed capability.

result_receipt_required: topology / hardware / firmware / control configuration digest
grid / load / source impedance and point-of-connection definition
HIL or physical test evidence class
instrument calibration IDs and measurement uncertainty
raw waveform digests and test procedure revision
acceptance threshold source and exact edition/agreement
non_claims: This matrix does not set universal performance thresholds.
It is not a substitute for licensed IEEE standards, local utility interconnection requirements or competent protection engineering.
A HIL/simulation pass is not a physical product qualification.
No equipment is authorized for energized construction or operation by this dataset.
